subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: At the decline stage of the product life cycle, a business is most likely to:
options: Charge a skimming price as a brand-new product
Launch the product for the first time
See falling sales and may withdraw the product or use an extension strategy
questions.explain: In decline, sales fall and the firm may withdraw the product or apply extension strategies to prolong its life.

questions.q: What is market segmentation?
options: Dividing a market into groups of customers with similar characteristics
questions.explain: Segmentation splits a market into groups (e.g. by age, income or lifestyle) so marketing can be targeted.

questions.q: Sampling in market research is used because:
options: Asking a representative group is quicker and cheaper than surveying the whole population
It is impossible to ask anyone at all
It avoids the need for any data
questions.explain: A sample lets a business gather views from a representative group rather than surveying everyone, saving time and money.

questions.q: Herzberg argued that factors such as pay and working conditions are:
options: Hygiene factors that prevent dissatisfaction but do not strongly motivate
The only thing that motivates employees
questions.explain: In Herzberg's theory, hygiene factors like pay and conditions stop dissatisfaction but do not actively motivate.

questions.q: Induction training is:
options: Always done away from the workplace
Training given to new employees when they start a job
questions.explain: Induction training introduces new employees to the business, their role and procedures.

questions.q: What is enterprise in a business context?
options: The skill of spotting an opportunity and taking the risk to act on it
questions.explain: Enterprise involves identifying a business opportunity and taking the risk of acting on it.

questions.q: On-the-job training means:
options: Watching online videos at home only
Learning while doing the actual job at the workplace
questions.explain: On-the-job training takes place at the workplace while the employee carries out the job.

questions.q: A business charges a high price to suggest premium quality and exclusivity. This pricing strategy is called:
questions.explain: Premium pricing sets a deliberately high price to signal a high-quality, exclusive product.

questions.q: Taylor's theory of motivation suggests workers are mainly motivated by:
options: Money and pay linked to output
questions.explain: Taylor argued workers are chiefly motivated by money, e.g. through piece-rate pay linked to output.

questions.q: In a partnership, profits are usually:
questions.explain: Partners typically share the profits (and losses) of the business according to their agreement.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a sales promotion?
options: A 'buy one get one free' offer
questions.explain: Sales promotions are short-term incentives such as BOGOF offers, discounts or free gifts to boost sales.

questions.q: How many levels are there in Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
questions.explain: Maslow's hierarchy has five levels: physiological, safety, social, esteem and self-actualisation.

questions.q: A business sets a low initial price to enter a market and attract customers. This pricing strategy is called:
questions.explain: Penetration pricing uses a low introductory price to gain market share quickly.

questions.q: In the Boston Matrix, a product with high market share in a high-growth market is called a:
questions.explain: A 'star' has a high share of a fast-growing market and usually needs investment to maintain its position.

questions.q: A decentralised structure can benefit a business because:
options: Local managers can make quicker decisions suited to local needs
No one is given any authority
Head office controls every small choice
questions.explain: Decentralisation passes decision-making to local managers, allowing faster decisions tailored to local conditions.

questions.q: A democratic leadership style involves:
options: The leader making all decisions alone
The leader involving employees in decision-making
questions.explain: A democratic leader consults and involves employees when making decisions.

questions.q: Cost-plus pricing works by:
options: Matching the price of the cheapest competitor
Always charging the lowest price in the market
Adding a percentage mark-up to the cost of making the product
Setting price based only on customer opinion
questions.explain: Cost-plus pricing adds a profit mark-up to the unit cost to set the selling price.

questions.q: In the Boston Matrix, a 'cash cow' is a product with:
options: Low share in a low-growth market
High share in a declining market only
Low share in a high-growth market
High share in a low-growth (mature) market
questions.explain: A cash cow has a high share of a low-growth market, generating steady cash with little extra investment.

questions.q: Secondary market research involves:
options: Using data that already exists, such as published reports
questions.explain: Secondary research uses existing data such as government statistics or market reports.

questions.q: What is a key benefit of strong branding for a business?
options: It removes the need for any marketing
It allows the business to charge higher prices and build customer loyalty
questions.explain: A strong brand builds customer loyalty and often allows a business to charge a premium price.

questions.q: Why might shareholders and employees have conflicting interests?
options: Shareholders may want higher profits while employees want higher wages
Both want the business to close
Neither group cares about the business
questions.explain: Higher wages can reduce profits, so shareholders' and employees' interests can conflict.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of market research?
options: To gather information about customers and the market to inform decisions
questions.explain: Market research collects information about customers and markets to help a business make better decisions.
